passage:
Students researched why their street was named Harbor Road, even though the sea was now far away.
Old maps showed that the coastline had once been closer. Over time, land was filled, roads were built, and the harbor moved.
The street name had become a fossil in language. It remembered a landscape that no longer existed.
Students made a display with old maps and current photos.
Residents were surprised to learn that an everyday name carried hidden geography.
A street name can seem ordinary until someone asks why it exists. Then it becomes a clue. Cities remember through words, even when the ground changes.
